options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Examine the precise distinction between projection completeness and monotone sequential completeness, looking for a structural theorem whose hypotheses match the definition in the problem. If such a theorem applies, the no-least-upper-bound requirement immediately excludes every positive increment.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Attempt a direct construction of the supremum using finite spectral approximations and joins of projections. The central issue would be showing that the resulting element is an upper bound in the ordinary operator order, not merely in spectral order.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor is monotone sequentially complete: every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements has a least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether completeness in the quasitracial metric, together with bounded monotonicity, guarantees convergence. Separate the metric-completeness theorem from the additional argument needed to show that the given sequence is Cauchy.

options.counterfactual: The 2-quasitrace extension rules out any infinite family of projections with uniformly positive quasitrace and uniformly bounded positive partial sums.
options.approach: Use rectangular matrices assembled from the projections to seek a dimension estimate that contradicts finiteness. Explicitly check every passage involving diagonal blocks, since quasitraces cannot be assumed to preserve diagonal pinching.

options.counterfactual: The 2-quasitrace extension rules out any infinite family of projections with uniformly positive quasitrace and uniformly bounded positive partial sums.
options.approach: Investigate whether bounded sums of projections allow extraction of subprojections that are mutually orthogonal and retain a fixed positive quasitrace. Such an extraction would contradict additivity on orthogonal projections without requiring general quasitrace additivity.

options.counterfactual: The 2-quasitrace extension rules out any infinite family of projections with uniformly positive quasitrace and uniformly bounded positive partial sums.
options.approach: Search the available proof notes for an applicable projection-packing or quasitracial exhaustion theorem and audit its proof. Once established, apply spectral cuts to the increments to obtain the forbidden projection family.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a bounded increasing sequence having constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Start from a concrete witness and investigate compression to corners, tracking both quasitrace normalization and upper bounds. The goal would be to determine whether the increment can be increased, rather than merely decreased by scalar multiplication.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a bounded increasing sequence having constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Study quasitracial ultraproducts of witnesses whose increments approach the supremum of the attainable values. Use a diagonal argument to test whether the limiting sequence still has no least upper bound, which could establish inclusion of the endpoint.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace and a bounded increasing sequence having constant positive quasitrace increments and no least upper bound.
options.approach: Analyze the endpoint one half using finite sums of three or more increments. Determine whether the resulting equalities of quasitrace values impose additional spectral constraints, without invoking unproved strict order preservation.
